To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“In the Fe|SCY|Au cell, the charge transfer electrode reactions are characterized by limiting currents and apparent exchange current densities that are strongly dependent on hydrogen partial pressure and temperature.
the apparent charge transfer coefficients, α a  and  α c, were found close to 0 and 1, respectively, and that the apparent reaction order,  q, was found close to 1/2, in most cases.
the charge transfer electrode kinetics at the Fe|SCY|Au cell are controlled by the hydrogen ad-atom or proton transport at the three phase boundaries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the charge transfer kinetics at the three phase H 2 –metal–SCY boundary in a solid electrolyte cell, and the effect of the operating parameters on the reaction kinetics.
the study of the charge transfer kinetics and mechanism at a three phase boundary in proton conducting solid electrolytes.
a better understanding of the charge transfer reaction taking place at a proton conducting solid electrolytic cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrode kinetics are controlled by a combination of charge transfer and mass transfer processes.

at low hydrogen partial pressures (1.3 and 3.1 kPa) at 700 °C, the charge transfer mechanism is the limiting step of the overall electrode reaction, while at high hydrogen partial pressures (4.6 and 5.8 kPA) at 700, 800 °C, and at all hydrogen partial pressures at 600 °C, the mass transport of hydrogen along the electrode/surface electrolyte interface, is the limiting step.
the reaction mechanism is a complex process that is affected by the experimental conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the charge transfer reaction at the H 2 –SCY–Fe three phase boundary can be described by a mechanism where the rate determining step involves the charge transfer reaction, which is coupled with the mass transfer of hydrogen species.
the reaction mechanism is not only dependent on the reaction conditions, but also on the nature and composition of the electrode material.

in the presence of limiting current densities, the charge transfer reaction at the three phase boundaries of the cell Fe|SCY|Au is controlled by the hydrogen diffusion along the electrode/solution interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrode reaction is not a pure charge transfer process, but it also involves the mass transport of hydrogen species.
the charge transfer kinetics at the three-phase boundary is strongly affected by the hydrogen partial pressure and the cell operating temperature.

electrode kinetic studies in solid electrolyte cells, can be used as a valuable tool for the determination of the charge transfer mechanism, and for the estimation of kinetic parameters, such as the apparent exchange current density and charge transfer coefficients.
